_README: THE OBLIGATIONS REGISTER — the single list of what must be true before V2 ships.
Findings live in several documents and the SAME obligation appears in more than one of them:
the ATP limit is a walk punch-list item, a red-line finding, an SQF clause and a queued build.
That is the defect this whole architecture is about — a fact in more than one place — happening
in our own documentation. This file gives each obligation exactly ONE owner, and lists every
finding that points at it under `sources`.
DERIVED FROM NOTHING. This register is hand-maintained on purpose: grouping findings into
obligations is judgement, not parsing. What IS mechanical is the check —
`node scripts/check-obligations.mjs` fails if any finding ID in the source documents is not
claimed by exactly one obligation here, or if this file claims an ID that does not exist.
So a new finding cannot be added to a document and quietly forgotten.
STATUS values:
open     — nothing built, nothing written. Needs a decision or a person.
drafted  — the document or design exists and is reviewable; not landed.
built    — code exists on the Track B branch, wired to nothing.
queued   — written out exactly in docs/v2/queued/, ready to land on main in one pass.
landed   — on main and deployed. Its queued file moves to docs/v2/landed/.
BUCKET (from audit-nc-triage.md):
A — ReadyDoc is the fix.  B — ReadyDoc makes it stick.  C — outside ReadyDoc.
doc — a change to a controlled document; no software involved.

obligations.title: Grade the ATP reading against PC #1's 35 RLU, and raise the re-clean on two failures
obligations.note: LANDED on main 27 Aug 2026. server/atp-limits.js owns the 35 RLU, registered with controlled.js so the number cannot be edited in the app; grading is asymmetric (an over-limit reading forces fail, an in-limit one never upgrades what the filer chose); the limit is stored on the record it graded (sanitation_records.atp_limit). Two consecutive failed swabs raise the re-clean work order — the plant's rule, because one high reading can be the swab rather than the line. Closing that task also had to be fixed: closeRecleanTasksFor matched the 72-hour task by exact title, so a passing clean left the ATP task open. AtpLimitHint gives the operator live EN/ES feedback and enforces nothing. Verified on a fresh DB: 24 unit assertions and seven end-to-end scenarios. SQF-06 (validating the number itself) moved to OBL-27; SQF-09 (naming the test method) moved to OBL-15, where the plan is reissued — neither is something software can discharge.

obligations.title: Enter the four preventive controls into haccp_ccps and guard their limits
obligations.note: Transcription pending verification against the PDF by Lowry, Daniela and Carol. Seeder call and the api/haccp.js edit guard are queued for main.

obligations.title: Banned and prohibited substance control — SOP, annual list review, purchasing check
obligations.note: THREE NONCONFORMANCES, ONE SOP. The draft exists as SOP-DRAFT-BSC. Needs: the SOP written and numbered (C); an annual quality schedule for the list review (B); one line on FORM 204-01 for the purchasing check, which requires a DCR (A).

obligations.title: 21 CFR Part 11 validation package for ReadyDoc
obligations.note: The only nonconformance that names ReadyDoc. Intended use and scope, a Part 11 gap assessment, IQ/OQ/PQ for the system, test scripts with recorded results approved by Quality, and software change control. SQF-23 adds one the supplements code requires and the Food Manufacturing code does not: software and electronic records backed up remote from the site's system, documented. Interlocks with OBL-05.

obligations.title: Change control covering processes, software, utility and physical plant
obligations.note: controlled.js is already a real gate for form definitions and acceptance criteria — widen it. Adds QC approval on every change, which the current DCR flow does not enforce. Software change control is required by this AND by OBL-04: build once. Wave 2 sized both halves. W2-12: SOP 434's title names chemicals, equipment AND services; ReadyDoc records only chemicals (approved_chemicals is a real approval record with approved_by/at and review_due) and has no equipment or services approval record at all — the software has the same scope gap the auditor found in the document. W2-13: controlled.js IS a working change-control gate with an approval and an audit trail, over exactly three things (QMS form definitions, scale tolerances, the ATP limit); it sees no process, utility, physical-plant or software change. W2-14: 111.130(e) wants QC approval and the DCR flow enforces Document Control only. W2-15: SOP 700 may also govern chemical approval. Interlock with OBL-04 — software change control is named in 4.4.39 too. The wording pass confirmed the auditor needs no argument: SOP 434's scope is chemicals, equipment and services, written as one approval path each, and processes/software/utilities/physical plant appear NOWHERE (W2-35) — so closing this is a rewrite of the scope, not an addendum. W2-33 adds a complication found only by reading SOP 421: IT ALSO REQUIRES A CHANGE-CONTROL SYSTEM for qualified equipment and never cites 434, so widening change control has to reconcile the two documents. W2-36: the SOP is titled '...APPROVAL FORM' and the form it requires has no number, so a record cannot say which it was filed against. W2-37 is the closest ReadyDoc comes to satisfying a Wave 2 SOP as written — approved_chemicals is three columns short of the tracking number, approval number and expiry the SOP requires. W2-14 RESOLVED by reading: the SOP does make the QA/QC Manager the final approver, so the document is fine and the DCR flow is the gap.

obligations.title: Master manufacturing record per formulation and batch size, then the executed batch record
obligations.note: The standing headline gap, now with a nonconformance. FORM 413-1 is the plant's own number, on paper in MRPEasy today. Sequence: MMR first (it is the finding), BPR second. Links to the Production Log rather than replacing it. Also decides the absorb-or-API-connect question.

obligations.title: Environmental monitoring result record, with trending
obligations.note: Three independent routes to one conclusion: the walk found no record path, the auditor found the testing was not done, SQF requires results tracked and trended. Schedule also needs location rotation and a documented method for elevated results (2.4.8.2). Wave 2 found the third gap and it is the decisive one. W2-16: completing a quality schedule writes work_orders and quality_schedules and NOTHING else, so a swab never taken and a swab whose result went nowhere are indistinguishable — the auditor's finding in software terms. W2-17: FORM 604-01's alert and action limits are transcribed faithfully in emp-site-list.js and graded against nothing, which is the ATP 35 RLU state exactly, and OBL-01 is now the working template for the fix. W2-18: the form's WATER section has no EMP schedule at all — monthly potable water (TAB, coliforms, free chlorine, each with limits) is served instead by a pre-existing 'Tap Water Testing' schedule that names no test, cites no limit and never references the form; the room-air row is the same story. Two mechanisms for one requirement is how one goes quiet. The wording pass found the most serious single finding in Wave 2 and it is not about software: FOUR BROKEN CROSS-REFERENCES INSIDE THE OOS ESCALATION (W2-39), including 5.3.5 citing itself — so the Zone 1 product-contact positive procedure instructs the reader to follow the Zone 1 procedure, and the water procedure is sent to Zone 1 rather than to the general escalation. Ten-minute fix. W2-40 is a hard dependency on any build here: the SOP states MONTHLY sampling for zones 2-4 while deferring frequency to FORM 604-01, which says semi-annual/annual/quarterly — and the six seeded EMP schedules follow the form, so if the SOP is right every zone schedule is at the wrong cadence. SETTLE THAT BEFORE BUILDING. W2-41: the OOS form is never named and the EMPRCA report has no controlled number. W2-42: 'the Quality Manager and Quality Manager' leaves the corrective-action decision authority unstated. W2-43/44/45: three roles used but never established, an annual verification written as 'should' and then relied on as fact, and two recurring obligations (semi-annual MRB trend review, annual baseline mapping) with no generator. NOTE the plant confirmed 27 Aug that the tap water sampling IS being done and logged in Quality Schedules — so this obligation buys the evidence, the grading and the trend the SOP itself demands (5.6, 5.7), not the work.

obligations.title: Supplier qualification records — questionnaire, risk evaluation, disposition, certificate expiry
obligations.note: SOP 404 exists; the records do not. FORM 404-1/404-2 marked keychain and producing nothing. Expiring-certificate pattern exists in `certifications`; approval pattern in `qms_records`. FSP-25 (FSVP) rides here: if any ingredient is imported it is the same programme. Wave 2 measured the gap: there is no supplier record in ReadyDoc of ANY kind (W2-05) — approved_chemicals holds chemicals, certifications holds PEOPLE (person_name NOT NULL), supply_orders is office purchasing. The auditor's three named suppliers had nowhere to be filed. W2-06 adds the half the title now covers: no laboratory record at all, coa_requests.lab_name is free text, '17025' appears nowhere, and coa-grade.js already reasons from 'it is the accredited party' — a principle resting on a fact nothing holds. W2-07 is the decision to take before building (new table vs widening certifications) and W2-08 is Daniela's (do FORM 404-1/404-2 become ReadyDoc screens or stay with Keychain). The wording pass found the document half is thinner than the software half. V4 puts laboratories in the title and adds a procedure section, and NEVER UPDATES THE SCOPE (W2-24), which still reads 'suppliers of raw materials and packaging'. The entire laboratory programme is TWO SENTENCES naming no standard, no scope of accreditation, no expiry, no owner and no record (W2-25) — 'ISO certification' is not a requirement, and ISO 9001 is not evidence a lab can run the test; ISO/IEC 17025 per scope is. The SOP also cites FORM 404-3 (Vendor Audit Summary), which exists in neither the Master Index nor the DCR log (W2-26), while requiring the vendor audits it records. Plus: V4's footer still carries the old title (W2-27), 'QVS' and 'Qualified Supplier Database' are named and never defined (W2-28), and an ANNUAL vendor review is required with no schedule behind it (W2-29) — that is the 'ongoing performance review' leg of the module. DESIGNED 27 Aug (docs/v2/queued/supplier-qualification.md) and the LABORATORY HALF SPLIT OUT to OBL-28. Wave 2 put SOP 404 last on the build order on the strength of W2-25; that is true of the laboratory half ONLY. The supplier half of SOP 404 V4 §V is the best-specified of the four Wave 2 documents — pre-assessment steps, seven named risk criteria, three named dispositions, QVL, emergency vendors, monitoring, disqualification — and is buildable from the document as it stands. Shape: suppliers + supplier_qualifications (one row per vendor PER PERIOD, which is what the plant's own vendor/2025 and vendor/2026 folders already are) + supplier_materials + supplier_files on R2. The risk criteria and dispositions are TRANSCRIBED from the SOP, not typed. on_qvl is a MIRROR of the disposition, never an input. Two importers, both existing patterns: Jake's spreadsheet is one TARGETS entry in imports.js; the per-vendor zip is the scanned-tests pattern with the PATH doing the work the filename did. THE ARCHIVE IS TOO BIG FOR ANY EXISTING PATH (media.js caps non-video at 25 MB, the training zip importer at 400 MB in memory) — the parser is built and tested against a PATH LISTING, and the bytes go in per vendor or per year through the app. Also closes a gap nothing had named: coa_specifications is keyed on item_number with NO supplier link and coa_requests records a lab but never a vendor, so ReadyDoc cannot today answer 'which supplier's material failed this test' — the question SOP 404 §V.E vendor monitoring is built on.

obligations.title: Raw material and finished product specifications as approved documents, with a release gate
obligations.note: Forward half only — the historical gap cannot be fixed by software. Same defect class as the ungraded ATP reading: a test with no active specification quietly passes. Identity by organoleptic alone is not acceptable.

obligations.title: Allergen management programme
obligations.note: SQF 2.8.1 is Mandatory with a six-part content list, including workplace allergens from locker rooms, vending machines and lunchrooms, and food-grade lubricants. 2.8.1.5 requires validation AND verification of allergen cleaning — that is PC #2. 2.8.1.10 requires allergen rework to be identified and traceable.

obligations.title: Food fraud plan, separate from food defense
obligations.note: The largest single gap the SQF pass found. 2.7.2 is its own Mandatory clause: methods/responsibility/criteria, a mitigation plan, staff training, and an annual review with gaps and corrective actions documented. The substance is in Protocol 001 §3A; the structure is not.

obligations.title: GMP observation record, and footwear control in GMP areas
obligations.note: The only finding about behaviour rather than paperwork, and the only one about product safety today rather than evidence. The behaviour is fixed by Operations now. The record that catches recurrence is the dormant checklist_templates engine, already typed `gmp`.

obligations.title: IQ/OQ/PQ per equipment, surfaced on the readiness checklist
obligations.note: Performing the qualification is engineering work. Holding it is three more derived steps on equipment-readiness.js, each satisfied by an attached protocol — which makes 'which machines are unqualified' answerable on a screen. Wave 2 confirmed the starting point: 'IQ', 'OQ' and 'PQ' appear NOWHERE in the codebase (W2-09), and equipment-readiness.js derives ten steps per machine of which none is qualification — so 'which machines are unqualified' is not a question the app can be asked. W2-10: no 421-series form number exists for a qualification protocol. W2-11: this is the cheapest of the four Wave 2 SOPs to close — three derived steps on a pattern that already carries its own roll-up and badges. The wording pass produced the finding that decides how NC 4.5.8 is answered: SOP 421's own scope is 'all NEW AND SIGNIFICANTLY MODIFIED facilities and equipment' (W2-31), so read strictly it does not require what the auditor found missing on equipment already in service. Either the SOP gains a retrospective-qualification clause or the plant argues scope against a finding already on the record — and no IQ/OQ/PQ checklist should be derived across 183 machines until that is decided. W2-32 sharpens W2-10: the SOP lists EIGHT record types and numbers none of them. W2-34: it requires approval from an 'Operations Manager' the document never establishes, and a periodic-review schedule with no interval stated.

obligations.title: Stability study, and link each product's expiry to it
obligations.note: Laboratory work over real time. SQF-24 sharpens it: the supplements code drops the Food Manufacturing code's 'or established by the site' fallback, so retention is anchored to shelf life with NO alternative basis — and that shelf life is itself under nonconformance 4.6.21.

obligations.title: Reissue Protocol 003 — Food Safety Plan V5
obligations.note: The document changes. Includes the three internal contradictions raised as a DCR (FSP-02/03 sit under OBL-16 because they change a control, not just wording). X-04 is the Scope and Normative References section, which OBL-18 depends on.

obligations.title: Correct the two preventive controls the plan states wrongly
obligations.note: Separated from OBL-15 because these change what a control IS, not how it reads: the Rework row cites a metal detector the plant does not have, and the screens frequency differs between the chart and the Process Description. Both must settle before OBL-02's transcription is final.

obligations.title: Reissue Protocol 001 — Food Defense Plan V3
obligations.note: SQF-19 (contractor access) is owned by OBL-21, which builds the record; the plan text follows from it. SQF-20 CORRECTS FDP-24: 2.7.1.4 requires the plan reviewed AND TESTED annually, and the plan commits to a mock incident every two years. SQF-15 (name the senior manager responsible) is required and trivially fixed.

obligations.title: Document reference graph and the fan-out on re-issue
obligations.note: BLOCKED ON OBL-15 AND OBL-17. Neither plan cites another document by number, so the graph would find nothing. The plan revision must land first — building the mechanism over an empty graph produces something indistinguishable from broken. W2-19 names the best candidate after the two plans: SOP 604 governs a programme carried out under SOP 600 (Air Monitoring V1), SOP 601 (Microbial Surface Testing V1) and SOP 608 (Surface ATP Swab Testing V4). 608 went V1 to V4 over ten months while 604 stayed at V2 and nothing in the register says whether 604 was re-checked. One governing document, three governed, an obvious question on every revision — but it still needs SOP 604's text to confirm it cites the other three by number, which is exactly what neither plan turned out to do (D-027). W2-46 answers the [verify in source] on W2-19 and changes the sequencing question. SOP 604 CITES SOP 600 and SOP 601 BY NUMBER, and SOP 404 cites SOP 607 — so unlike Protocol 003 and Protocol 001, which cite nothing at all (D-027), the registry's SOPs are a usable corpus for the reference graph. 604 does NOT cite SOP 608, the one of its three spokes that has moved four revisions while 604 stayed at V2, and relies on the Material Review Board throughout without citing SOP 412. The graph may not have to wait on the plan revision after all.

obligations.title: Food defense mock incident — annually, with a form and a record
obligations.note: mock_recalls with a different checklist. SQF 2.7.1.4 sets the cadence at ANNUAL, not the two years the plan states — see OBL-17. Records of both the review and the test are required.

obligations.title: Add a food defense section to Form 403-01
obligations.note: The internal audit is named as the food defense plan's verification and its nineteen sections contain none. Changing what an internal audit asks is a DCR — audit-checklist.js is not user-editable by design.

obligations.title: Visitor and contractor access log
obligations.note: SQF 2.7.1.2(vii) names site personnel, CONTRACTORS and visitors. The kiosk pattern fits a lobby sign-in exactly. Contractors are the group most likely to be on site unescorted with tools.

obligations.title: A per-run trigger for run-boundary controls
obligations.note: DEFERRED BY DECISION (D-019). Every generator is a calendar and three of four preventive controls fire per production run. Architecture move 05, after the audit. The record leg (OBL-01) is what an auditor asks for; this is the refinement.

obligations.title: Rework and pest control programmes
obligations.note: Two of the four absent programmes from the walk. Allergen is OBL-10 and GMP observation is OBL-12; these two have no home yet. Rework is a named process step in Protocol 003 with three controls applied to it.

obligations.title: Two single-leg fixes: a form number for calibration, a generator for mock recall
obligations.note: Calibration has a record and no form number. Mock recall has a record and a form and no generator — its cadence is reported, not raised.

obligations.title: Confirm which Keychain forms produce records today
obligations.note: ANSWERED IN PART, 27 Aug 2026: the SQF code question is settled — the Dietary Supplement Manufacturing code Edition 9 is the one that applies, it is now in the reference registry as REF-SQF-DSC-9, and every Part 5 clause was re-verified against it. What remains: none of the seven keychain-marked forms is producing records, and the absorb-or-API-connect exit is OBL-06.

obligations.title: Mechanical sweep of the whole document registry
obligations.note: Extend doc-consistency.js with the rules generalised from the plan red-line — approved-but-unsigned, revision disagreement, unspecified retention, cites-nothing, section and page arithmetic, spelling. Output is a queue with dismissals, not a document. Wave 2 gave this obligation its first concrete rules and they are not spelling rules. W2-01: two controlled documents the auditor read (SOP 421, SOP 434) have NO row in the 159-row DCR log — no new-document row, no revision row. W2-02: SOP 404 is V4 with a widened title in practice and V3 under the old title in the log. W2-03: SOP 604's effective date is eight months after its last change request. W2-04 is the structural cause of all three — the DCR log imports into the QMS register while documents live in sop_documents, two lists nothing reconciles in either direction. Add both directions as sweep rules ('in the log, absent from the registry' and its inverse); they would have caught W2-01 and W2-02 without anybody reading anything. The wording pass added the rules the sweep should carry, and every one is now evidenced on four real documents rather than argued: NONE of the four is signed (W2-20 — both approval blocks empty in all four), EVERY one disagrees with its own revision history about its current revision date (W2-21 — SOP 434 by ten months, SOP 404 V3 by thirteen), the SOP 404 file holds TWO complete revisions in one document (W2-22), and section numbering is broken in three of four (W2-23). 'Approved but unsigned' and 'header vs revision-history disagreement' are now the two highest-yield sweep rules.

obligations.title: Validate the 35 RLU ATP limit, and re-validate it annually
obligations.note: Split out of OBL-01 when the grading landed. SQF 2.4.3.11 and 2.5.1.1(ii) require the critical limit to be VALIDATED — evidence that 35 RLU is the right number for these surfaces and this instrument — and re-validated at least annually. ReadyDoc now grades against the number; it cannot justify it, and an app enforcing an unvalidated limit is precisely the finding. Two separate pieces of work: the validation study (outside ReadyDoc, QA with the instrument manufacturer's guidance), and then the annual re-validation, which once the study exists is a Quality Schedule like any other cadence. Until the study exists, atp-limits.js should say the limit is transcribed from Protocol 003 and not yet validated — which is what it says.

obligations.title: Laboratory qualification — write the programme, then hold it
obligations.note: Split out of OBL-08 on 27 Aug because the two halves are blocked on different things. SOP 404 V4 added 'and Laboratory' to the title and a section G of TWO SENTENCES — 'Laboratories will be approved upon receipt of ISO certification. An audit report will be requested and kept on file.' It names no standard (ISO 9001 is a management-system certificate, not evidence a lab can run the test; ISO/IEC 17025 per SCOPE OF ACCREDITATION is the one that matters), no expiry, no re-approval, no owner, no form and no record — and V4 never updated §II SCOPE, which still covers only suppliers of raw materials and packaging (W2-24). Meanwhile coa_requests.lab_name is free text, '17025' appears nowhere in the codebase, and coa-grade.js already grades every result on the reasoning that 'it is the accredited party' (W2-06). BUILDING A REGISTER AGAINST THE CURRENT WORDING WOULD ENCODE 'ISO certification' AS A REQUIREMENT, WHICH IS NOT ONE. The document comes first; the register is small once it exists.
